title: Multi-timescale streaming batcher with KV-pressure adaptive policies
creator: Ethan Collins
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response length workloads (chat, search+context, code completion) cause our continuous streaming batcher to either: 1) over-reserve KV memory for long-horizon dialogues (wasting GPU memory and increasing OOM risk), or 2) evict too aggressively and thrash for long contexts, causing latency spikes and quality regressions. We need a scheduling policy that adapts across timescales so short bursts get low-latency slots while long contexts retain KV residency without unbounded memory growth.

Proposal: Implement a multi-timescale streaming batcher that multiplexes requests into three soft-timescale lanes (micro, horizon, epoch) and combines: 1) per-request KV-reservation budgets derived from token-length forecasts, 2) KV-pressure signals from realtime GPU allocator telemetry, and 3) an adaptive warmup/decay policy that pins hot KV entries for a configurable tenure. The scheduler will:
- Classify incoming requests by predicted response length and recent reuse (hot prefix) into micro (<=32 tokens), horizon (33-512), epoch (>512) lanes.
- Use a token-forecast model (lightweight heuristic + smoothed EWMA of recent seq-lengths) to assign initial KV_reserve_size.
- Allocate soft KV reservations as fractions of a lane-specific quota; quotas adapt every N seconds based on measured KV occupancy and freeable slab pages.
- When global KV-pressure > threshold, throttle micro-lane coalescing (favor latency over coalescing) and trigger opportunistic prefix evictions in epoch lane with LRU+age bias.
- Provide a manual override: tenant-level kv_reserve_multiplier (for Dedicated/Private customers).

Acceptance criteria / metrics:
- End-to-end 95th latency for micro-lane requests should not regress >5% compared to baseline.
- Mean token-cost per response should decrease by >=6% on mixed workloads (25/50/25 split micro/horizon/epoch) versus current static reservation policy.
- OOM events attributable to KV overcommit should drop to zero in 72-hour stress runs.
- Quality checks: regression in model output due to eviction should be <=1% on predefined eval prompts (run via Checkout-evals).

Implementation plan:
1) Telemetry: expose KV-residency, slab fragmentation, and freeable-pages metrics from allocator (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1243).
2) Scheduler prototype: add lane classification and soft-reserve accounting in batcher codepath behind runtime flag flag_multi_timescale_batcher. Implement conservative heuristics first (no eviction), measure.
3) Policy layer: implement adaptive quota controller and eviction policy (LRU+age bias, with configurable tenure).
4) Perf experiments: run 72-hour stress runs on staging clusters with mixed-length traces from production replay (trace-id list in Confluence).
5) Rollout: start Canary on Dedicated cluster pool A, monitor latency/cost/ooms for 48h, then ramp.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Why multi-timescale lanes? Observed tail amplification when long contexts share slots with short requests; lanes allow tailored coalescing vs latency trade-offs.
- Soft reservations instead of hard: avoids global stalls while signalling expected residency.
- Prefetch vs eviction: we prefer keeping hot prefixes (to avoid quality regressions) and evict lower-value cold entries under pressure.

Instrumentation & dashboards:
- New dashboard panels: kv.total_resident_tokens, kv.freeable_pages, kv.fragmentation_ratio, batcher.lane_latency_p50/p95, batcher.kv_pressure_events.
- Alert: kv_pressure_events > 5 in 10m -> page on-call infra.

Rollout guardrails:
- Feature gated by runtime flag and tenant override.
- Canary policy limits: start with kv_reserve_multiplier=0.8 and strict logging.

comments: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: scoped scope and owners. Decided to prototype with 3 lanes (micro/horizon/epoch). Ethan ran initial replay to validate classification thresholds.
2026-03-02 - Telemetry PR merged (allocator/pull/89). Added kv.freeable_pages and kv.fragmentation_ratio metrics. These were missing previously and are vital for quota adaptation.
2026-03-04 - Proto deployed to staging behind flag. Early results: micro-lane p95 latency +3%, token-cost -4%. Behavior under high write workloads shows KV fragmentation causing slower recovery.

2026-03-06 - Design review with Reliability and ML (notes: prefer age-biased eviction, require eval-run after eviction to check quality regressions). Action: add LRU+age hybrid and run Checkout-evals before canary.

2026-03-09 - Benchmarks: 24h mixed-trace run on a 8-GPU staging pool. Observed 12% reduction in mean token-cost when using adaptive quotas, OOMs reduced by 70% vs baseline. Need longer run for tail stability.
2026-03-10 - PR opened for scheduler changes (runtime/pull/1248). CI flaky on memory allocator integration test; investigating alignment issues with slab accounting (assigned to Priya).
2026-03-12 - UX sync: Console team will add per-tenant kv_reserve_multiplier setting and a read-only graph for lane distribution. We will include defaults for hosted customers.
Next steps: complete allocator alignment fix, run 72-hour replay, add eviction-quality evals, and prepare canary run on Dedicated pool A with strict logging enabled.
